//: Phase 0 decision 2 (IP-unified-architecture.md §13.2): the stack stays JS +
Python, NOT TypeScript. The rationale for TS was real — it would have caught
the [div,sin,cos] vs {order,sin,cos} confusion at compile time — so the
safety is replaced rather than dropped: JSDoc annotations plus checkJs give
genuine type checking and editor support with no build step.
This also supplies the type information @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises
needs (§4), which cannot work on plain JS without it.
Scope is packages/ only. src/script.js is 64,714 lines of pre-migration code
and would drown the signal; it joins as Phase 8 extracts from it.
maxNodeModuleJsDepth is 0 because `exclude` does not cover files reached
through imports — without it TypeScript walks into node_modules/punycode.
types:[node] lets the test harness use console/process/URL. It also makes
Node globals type-legal inside physics/src, which is intentional: the actual
purity rule is enforced by no-restricted-globals and the purity test, both of
which have been shown to reject violations. Types are not the gate here.
